annotations.title: Save a model to your account

description: Saves a model to your Neumann account so you can come back to it instead of describing it again. A saved model is called a graph: its uncertain inputs, the formulas that combine them, and the links between them. Use this when the user will revisit this model -- a budget, a plan, a business case they will update -- or when you want to re-analyse it later without resending it; for a one-off question, pass the model inline to run_monte_carlo_simulation and save nothing. Omit graph_id to save a new graph. Pass the graph_id of a graph you saved before to replace that same graph with this version; the earlier versions are kept, so replacing is not losing anything. An input may be saved before it has a distribution, so you can build a draft model over a conversation; a graph with such an input cannot be run or analysed until each input has one. It returns the graph_id to use later, the version_id of the version it just stored, the name, and when it was last updated. Use that graph_id with get_graph to read the model back, with rank_inputs_by_impact or summarize_outcome_scenarios in place of an inline graph, and with delete_graph to remove it. run_monte_carlo_simulation does not take a graph_id: read the graph with get_graph and pass it inline. It needs a Neumann account: send your key, or your signed-in token, in the Authorization header as a Bearer credential. No Neumann tool takes an api_key argument. Cost: free -- it debits no credits and spends none of your free daily runs -- but it needs an account; an anonymous caller gets authentication_required.

graph.description: The model to save: its uncertain inputs (root_nodes), the formulas over them (calc_nodes), the links between them (edges) and the run settings (run_params). The same shape run_monte_carlo_simulation takes, except that an input may be saved before it has a distribution: give it distribution_type null and distribution_params {}. A graph with such an input cannot be run until you give it one. Only this outline is published here: the full schema is on run_monte_carlo_simulation's graph parameter, and the neumann://catalog resource lists every distribution and formula function. Neumann checks the model against that full schema when you call this tool and names any problem.
